notes: One Epson service manual covers the Stylus CX4300, CX4400, CX5500, CX5600, DX4400 and DX4450, so the electrical and mechanical details apply to the whole family; the 100-120 V and 220-240 V models have different mains inputs. Parts are named by function and stated rating, because the manual gives no parts list or part numbers.

gaps: The manual says it has no exploded diagrams or parts list (section 7.2) and points to a separate Service Parts Information list that is not in this copy, so no OEM part numbers are claimed.
Table 2-1 gives a CR motor coil resistance of 28.8 ohm, but the note under table 3-1 says the resistance varies between poles and cannot be used to test the motor. Recorded as stated.

A6628 is named as drive IC for the CR and PF motors and L6219 for the scanner motor (motor tables); table 2-5 lists main-board motor drivers U7 (CR/PF) and U6 (scanner) without chip numbers, so the pairing is by function.
No datasheet is linked for A6628 or L6219; the ST product page for L6219 timed out on two attempts, and no page for the exact part A6628 was found.
The scanner motor inductance is given as TBD, and its table 3-1 resistance carries a T.B.D. mark; the inductance is not recorded.
The power supply board has input ratings and a +42 VDC output but no output current or power, so no a or w value is set.
Springs, gears, belts, rods and the glass are named without sizes or materials.
The 100-120 V and 220-240 V models share one manual; the power supply row gives both input ranges.
method: Epson Stylus CX4300/CX4400/CX5500/CX5600/DX4400/DX4450 Service Manual, SEMF07-004 (Epson, copyright 2007, Revision A), 129-page PDF from Internet Archive item manualzilla-id-7408824. A user upload, not Epson's own host; the cover and every page header name the model family.

Sections used: 1.2.2 and 1.2.4 (scanner and power input specifications), 2.2 to 2.4 (printer mechanism, scanner, power supply and main board, tables 2-1 to 2-5), table 3-1 and the troubleshooting tables (pp. 40, 46), 4.6 and 4.8 (disassembly), 6.1 (lubrication), 7.1 and 7.2 (connectors, parts list).
The Internet Archive item page was read for the upload details.

comps.spec: CR (carriage) motor: brushed DC motor, drive voltage +42 V +/-5% at the driver, coil resistance 28.8 ohm +/-10%, inductance 20.1 mH +/-25%, PWM constant-current drive, driver IC A6628; its pinion gear drives the CR timing belt (section 2.2.2.1, table 2-1; section 4.6.4)
comps.loc: Fixed to the main frame with two screws (section 4.6.4)

comps.spec: PF (paper feed) motor: 4-phase 48-pole PM stepping motor, drive voltage +42 V +/-5%, 4.3 ohm +8/-12% per phase at 20 C, inductance 5.5 mH +/-20%, bipolar constant-current drive, driver IC A6628; the spec also covers the ASF and ink pump drive; three screws hold it (tables 2-2, 3-1; section 4.6.13)

Scanner motor: PM stepping motor, drive voltage 42 V DC, coil resistance 37 ohm +/-10% per phase at 25 C, PWM drive, open-loop control, driver IC L6219; the motor unit is held by three screws (section 2.3.1.2, table 2-4; section 4.8.3)
CR encoder sensor, part of the carriage unit, and the CR scale that sits in its slit; the scale is released from the slit when it is removed (sections 2.2.2 and 4.6.3)

CIS (contact image sensor) assembly on the scanner carriage: CIS board with sensing elements across the scan width, a rod lens array and red, green and blue LEDs; the scanner specification gives the sensor as CIS (sections 1.2.2, 2.3.1.1, 4.8.2)
CR timing belt, driven by the pinion gear of the CR motor; pressing the driven pulley holder slackens the belt for removal (sections 2.2.2 and 4.6.4)
Scanner timing belt that carries the scanner carriage unit, driven by the scanner motor (section 2.3.1.2); a spring-loaded driven pulley releases the belt when pushed (section 4.8.3)
Scanner carriage shaft, labelled in the scanner mechanism figure (figure 2-3); the CIS carrier also rides on a guide rail of the lower scanner housing, which is greased (sections 4.8.2 and 6.1.3)
Extension spring 3.289, released from a main frame hook when the CR scale is removed (section 4.6.3); compression spring 2.51 between the ASF frame and the hopper (troubleshooting table, p. 40)
Spur gears named in the manual: spur gear 59.6 on the EJ roller (section 4.6.8), spur gear 36 in the EJ frame assembly (troubleshooting table, p. 46), spur gear 13.5 on the PF roller (section 4.6.12)

Power supply board (ASSY POWER 110V/220V): flyback converter supplying +42 VDC to the drive line; mains input 100-120 VAC (100-120 V model) or 220-240 VAC (220-240 V model), 50-60 Hz; its cable plugs into J1 on the main board; one screw holds it (sections 1.2.4, 2.4.1, 4.6.7, 7.1)
Switching FET QF1 on the power supply board, which does the switching in the primary circuit of the flyback converter (section 2.4.1)
Drive IC A6628, named for the CR motor and the PF motor (tables 2-1 and 2-2); the main board's motor driver U7 handles the CR/PF motors (table 2-5)
Driver IC L6219, named for the scanner stepping motor (table 2-4); the main board's motor driver U6 drives the scanner motor (table 2-5)
CPU-ASIC U3 on the main board, based on an H8S/2674 CPU, 24 MHz, 3.3 V and 1.8 V (table 2-5)
Serial flash U5 on the main board, 4 Mbit, 3.3 V, stores the printer program (table 2-5)
Document glass in the upper scanner housing, named in the scanner image-quality troubleshooting and in the maintenance section (sections 3.3.1, 4.8.1 and 6.1)
